source_xy_policy: Keep the existing bounded x and y axes at extent 3, their coordinates, initial empty cells, X-first turn order, and empty-cell placement rule. Do not add gravity.
neighborhood: For winning lines, use all straight three-cell directions through the cube: three axis directions, six face-diagonal directions, and four body-diagonal directions. These define 49 distinct winning lines: 27 axis lines, 18 face diagonals, and 4 body diagonals. Placement itself has no neighborhood restriction.
movement: On a turn, the current player places their mark at any empty (x,y,z) cell. Reject an occupied cell or a placement after the game ends without changing state. Players continue alternating unless the placement ends the game. Restart resets all 27 cells and the turn to X; quit remains a host command.
outcomes: After each legal placement, a player wins if their marks fill any of the 49 straight three-cell lines. Check the win before the draw. If all 27 cells are occupied with no winning line, the result is a draw.
presentation: Show the board as the engine-owned continuous cube volume, with X and O in their cells and the existing turn, win, or draw status. Do not split the cube into panels.
input: Clicking a cell supplies its full (x,y,z) coordinate. The engine's existing '[' and ']' keys and on-screen buttons select depth for picking inner cells. Keep restart and quit bindings.
z_equals_one_tests: With z at extent 1, the same x and y placements, turns, and occupied-cell rejections must behave as in the Source.
With z at extent 1, only the Source's eight rows, columns, and diagonals can win; a full board without a line is a draw.

z_gt_one_tests.name: same x and y on different layers are distinct cells
